static_traits.name: Zhang Ruowei
static_traits.medical_history: No significant physical illness; no prior psychotherapy; no similar psychological problems before
static_traits.language_features: Clear expression, fairly good logic, highly cooperative, normal speech rate, slightly nervous and doubtful

basic_info.main_problem: I believe I am ordinary at dance and have no skill at all; this belief leads to self-doubt and low confidence.
basic_info.core_demands: Persistent negative feelings have affected my enjoyment of dance and my overall confidence; I hope that by challenging negative cognitions, gathering evidence, and reframing my perspective, I can shift from 'I have no skill' to 'I am gradually improving through practice and enjoying the process'.
growth_experiences: Started attending dance classes a year ago. During a class showcase, other students could complete advanced movements fairly perfectly, but he did not succeed, and felt out of place and ashamed. Afterwards, he frequently compared himself with others in class, saw others as more confident and skilled, and gradually formed a self-evaluation pattern of 'I am ordinary, have no skill, and am not good enough', which recurs every time he dances or thinks about dancing.

special_situations.event: During the class showcase, other students could complete advanced movements while he did not succeed
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I cannot complete the movements as perfectly as my classmates, it means I have no talent and I am not good enough
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Doubles practice but focuses excessively on errors, mentally dismissing positive feedback to avoid disappointment
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I am not suited to dancing / I have no skill at all

special_situations.event: Receives positive feedback from the instructor or classmates in class (such as 'you are improving', 'you did that move very well')
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: Only a performance completely without errors is worthy of recognition; others cannot see my real errors, so praise is not credible
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Ignores praise, fixates on shortcomings and flaws
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: They are just being polite; I am actually very bad

special_situations.event: In dance class, sees classmates performing more confidently and skillfully
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I am not as good as them, it proves I am no good / I am not good enough
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Constantly compares with others, lowering self-evaluation
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I am not as good as them; I am not good enough

special_situations.event: Notices several of his own errors when practicing or reviewing his performance
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: Making mistakes equals failure; errors better represent my true level
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Repeatedly criticizes himself in his mind, reducing enjoyment of the process
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: As expected, I am no good

core_conflict.wish: Longing to be recognized, to have my progress seen, and to be accepted as a 'dancer'
core_conflict.fear: Fears that after exposing shortcomings they will be judged and humiliated, ultimately negated as 'not good enough'
defense_goal: Lowers expectations through self-deprecation and denying the positive side, avoiding disappointment and external judgment

object_relations.self_representation: A trainee/dancer who is not good enough and mediocre
object_relations.object_representation: Others (classmates / coach) are more excellent and potentially critical judges, who can only see the parts I did right

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When the counselor or others give positive feedback in class / conversation, encouraging them to review strengths and progress
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Believes the other person cannot see the 'real self' (that is, the mistakes and shortcomings), so praise is not credible (transference: projecting one's own negating experience onto the other's intentions)
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Negates praise in a tactful but firm tone, often using sentence patterns such as 'but' and 'actually I am still terrible'; the tone is rather cautious and restrained, emphasizing details of their own mistakes to weaken positive information.

manifestations: Having several close friends but not sharing feelings of self-doubt and inadequacy with them
Experiences feeling out of place and shame in the dance community, subjectively feeling estranged from others
Loves dance but persistent self-negation diminishes the enjoyment
outcomes: 对自我价值的质疑增多

contact_model.definition: The individual has a poor capacity for self-reflection and introspection, with excessive self-restriction and self-blame, and is overly cautious about contact, corresponding to 'autonomy'.
manifestations: 过度关注错误、苛责自己
Remains skeptical of praise and positive feedback; hard to accept them
When reviewing performance, lists problems more than acknowledging strengths

contact_model.definition: The individual attributes feelings they find hard to accept to others, corresponding to 'possession'. Language manifestations include: 'He is looking down on me', 'They want to exclude me', and so on
manifestations: Believes others only see the 'parts done right' and cannot see the 'real mistakes'
Attributing one's negative experience to others' insincere or perfunctory praise

positive_force: Having a stable love for and participation in dance (continuously attending classes)
Others have given positive feedback (evaluated as having improved and completing certain movements well)
Occasionally able to complete some movements, existing observable fragments of success
negative_force: Excessively comparing with others, forming a fixed narrative of 'I am not as good as them'
Disqualifies positive feedback and focuses on mistakes (mental filtering)
Overgeneralizing one or a few failures into overall incompetence

target_behavior.behavior: Self-negation and comparison with others in dance-related situations
antecedent: Seeing classmates perform more confidently and skillfully
target_behavior.core_reason: Comparison with peers activates the core belief 'I am not good enough' and generalizes a single failure into a judgment of overall ability
target_behavior.function: Avoiding being judged and the sense of failure, preventing expectations and pressure through self-deprecation
target_behavior.consequence: Decreased pleasure in dance, impaired motivation, overall confidence reduced

target_behavior.behavior: Disqualifying positive feedback (treating praise as insincere or mere politeness)
antecedent: Receiving praise, encouragement, or improvement feedback from coaches or peers
target_behavior.core_reason: The inner rule is 'only perfection deserves recognition', so positive evaluations are interpreted as unreal or disregarded
target_behavior.function: Maintaining harsh standards to gain a sense of control, avoid disappointment and exposure of inadequacy
target_behavior.consequence: Unable to form balanced cognition, reinforcing self-doubt and frustration experience
